purpose: Reproducible, idempotent application of session-4 food-identity enrichments: canonical aliases and reviewed gut-taxonomy attributes. Every entry resolves by canonical identity — safe to re-run; creates no duplicates.

aliasPatches.rationale: Dahi/perugu/thayir/mosaru/doi are the same canonical food as plain curd (set cultured yogurt, unstrained) — regional names + native scripts, not distinct identities.

taxonomyAttributes.evidence: Set curd is milk inoculated with live starter cultures (Lactobacillus/Lactococcus spp.), consumed unheated. Live-culture status applies to traditionally prepared/unpasteurized curd; heat-treated or long-stored products may differ — viability is preparation-level, documented convention, not strain/CFU-verified.

Kimchi is a lactic-acid-fermented vegetable preparation typically consumed unheated and unpasteurized. Shelf-stable/pasteurized packaged products may lack viable cultures — flag is conventional-prep level.
Miso is a fermented soybean paste; it is frequently consumed heated (miso soup), so live-culture viability at consumption is preparation-dependent — FERMENTED only, live cultures unknown.
Sauerkraut is fermented cabbage, but commercially canned/pasteurized products are heat-treated. Live-culture viability is product-dependent — FERMENTED only, live cultures unknown.
